entities.name: Silk Road
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: A network of overland trade routes (~130 BCE – 1453 CE) stretching from Chang'an (Xi'an) to the Mediterranean, carrying silk, spices, jade, glass, and ideas across 4,000 miles. Far more than a commercial corridor, it transmitted Buddhism to China, Islam to Central Asia, paper and gunpowder to Europe, plague to both ends, and connected every major civilization in Eurasia.

entities.name: The Silk Road
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary: A 4,000-mile network of trade routes connecting Chang'an (Xi'an) to Rome. Silk, spices, ideas, religions, and diseases traveled along it. No single trader traveled the full route.
